{"id":"mimid-1wgh.115","title":"Open for Mark: should a call room be fixed_membership?","description":"Raised while building bead mimid-1wgh.108 step 3 (Store::start_call).

THE TEXT. room-policy-04 §5's note: "A room can be both fixed_membership
and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a multi-media call
of clients in a Group DM." So §5 itself offers the fixed-membership shape
for a call room, and draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.1 repeats it.

WHAT STORE::START_CALL DOES TODAY: it does NOT set fixed_membership. The
call room has the default open membership and the default roles, so a
participant can be added to a call in progress.

THE ARGUMENT FOR FIXED: §5 names it, and a call whose membership cannot
change is a call whose media key cannot leak to a late joiner by a
member's mistake. It is also the only way to say "these people and no
others" in room policy.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why it is not set: §5 also says "only a
single fixed-membership room can exist for any unique set of
participants". mimid does not count parent-dependent rooms in that rule
(decision mimid-1wgh.110, proposed upstream as #59), so a fixed call room
IS constructible here and the test
a_fixed_call_room_may_hold_the_same_pair_as_its_direct_room proves two
of them can exist in one DM. But that is mimid's reading of a rule the WG
has not changed yet. On a hub that reads §5 as published, a
fixed-membership call room in a DM would be the only call that DM could
ever have, because the second one duplicates the first's participant set.
Not setting the flag is the reading that interoperates with both.

Secondary: a call among a subset cannot add the people it left out, and
"let me pull Carol in" is a thing people do on calls.

WHAT A DECISION WOULD CHANGE: one field in Store::start_call, plus
whether it takes an argument for it. Nothing in the keying: the media
secret comes from the group's epoch either way.

{"notes":"POINTER: "proposed upstream as #59" above means ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#43. #59 was closed as a duplicate of it (bead mimid-1wgh.37.110).
MARK DECIDED 2026-11-23: anyone in the call can add anyone else. Leave it
as built. No code change.

CHOSEN: the call room keeps the default roles, so role 2 "member" has
canAddParticipant and a participant can pull someone into a call in
progress. The hub's subset rule still stops them pulling in anyone who is
not in the parent chat, so a call can never reach outside the chat it
came from.

NOT CHOSEN:
- fixed_membership, which §5's note suggests. Rejected on interoperation:
  a hub reading §5 as published, without the parent-dependent exemption
  of decision mimid-1wgh.110, would refuse a frozen call room holding the
  same people as the DM, as a duplicate of the DM. Our own PR for that
  exemption (#43) is not merged.
- withholding canAddParticipant from role 2 and leaving it with the
  creator, so only whoever started the call could widen it. It was the
  recommendation here, and Mark chose the more permissive shape instead.

WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE: "hold on, let me get Carol" works, and any
participant can do it. A member who adds someone adds them to the call's
MLS group, which moves the epoch, which rolls the media secret
(draft-atwood-mimi-calls §4.4), so the person added cannot read the media
sent before they arrived. That property does not depend on this choice."}
Mark 2026-11-23: anyone in the call can add anyone else; leave it as built, no code change.
